bug_description.normalized: UPX's 64-bit ELF unpacker builds a 1-based `dt_table` from the file's PT_DYNAMIC entries. The staged witness reaches `elf_find_table_size(DT_SYMTAB, SHT_DYNSYM)` even though its dynamic table has no `DT_SYMTAB` entry, so `dt_table[DT_SYMTAB]` remains 0. Vulnerable code then indexes `dynseg[-1 + x_ndx]` without checking that zero sentinel first. In the reproduced run the resulting pre-table 8-byte read landed in a heap chunk already freed by earlier doctest setup, so ASan reported a heap-use-after-free READ.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled PT_DYNAMIC contents into parser state. After the witness is accepted as an ELF64 ET_DYN file and a PT_DYNAMIC program header is found, this assignment stores the file-backed dynamic-entry array in `dynseg` for subsequent tag inversion.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is the exact 12248-byte file with sha256 `1f15023f241827d2ecee608a2207cc5cedf1940f39dada21192f096277c3976e`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` writes those bytes to `/tmp/libfuzzer.<pid>` and calls `upx_main(3, {"upx", "-t", infilename})` (fuzzers/test_packed_file_fuzzer.cpp:24-43). Static inspection identifies the file as an ELF64 little-endian ET_DYN shared object whose dynamic section lacks `DT_SYMTAB`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Missing zero-entry guard. `dt_table` stores 1-based PT_DYNAMIC indices and leaves absent tags as 0. For the witnessed `elf_find_table_size(DT_SYMTAB, SHT_DYNSYM)` call, this line loads the zero sentinel from `dt_table[DT_SYMTAB]`, but vulnerable code does not stop when `x_ndx == 0` before indexing `dynseg[-1 + x_ndx]`.
root_cause.note: The fix confirms the missing obligation here by inserting `if (!x_ndx) { return 0; }` immediately before the next line.

sink.description: Closest project-code sink responsible for the invalid read. With `x_ndx == 0`, this statement forms `&dynseg[-1].d_val` and asks `get_te64()` to read 8 bytes immediately before the PT_DYNAMIC array.
sink.note: ASan's PC is the inlined helper chain `get_te64` -> `LEPolicy::get64` -> `get_ne64` at `src/bele.h:124`, but this line is the exact caller that supplies the invalid pre-table address.

parser_admitted.description: The witness passes into the 64-bit ET_DYN Linux ELF parser path before PT_DYNAMIC is scanned.

tainted_value_origin.description: First field read from the attacker-controlled PT_DYNAMIC array. Repeated over the witness entries, this loop never yields `DT_SYMTAB` before `DT_NULL`, so the derived lookup table retains the zero sentinel for that tag.

fine_trace.note: Maps the witness's PT_DYNAMIC segment inside `file_image` and stores the resulting attacker-controlled dynamic-entry array in `dynseg`.

Scans the attacker-supplied `Elf64_Dyn` tags and records each present in-range tag as a 1-based index in `dt_table`. `readelf -d` on the staged witness shows 17 entries ending at `DT_NULL` with no `DT_SYMTAB`, so `dt_table[DT_SYMTAB]` is never written and remains 0 from the constructor's zero-initialization.

After the earlier `DT_STRSZ` check succeeds, the parser still asks for the size of `DT_SYMTAB`. In this `-t` path `shdri` is unavailable, so `elf_find_table_size()` cannot use a section-header shortcut and must resolve the size from `dt_table` and `dynseg`.

Root cause. For this call `dt_type` is `DT_SYMTAB`, so `x_ndx` loads the zero sentinel from `dt_table[DT_SYMTAB]`. The function enters the `dt_type < DT_NUM` fallback and omits the required `if (!x_ndx) return 0` guard before indexing `dynseg[-1 + x_ndx]`.

With `x_ndx == 0`, the address expression becomes `&dynseg[-1].d_val`, so `get_te64()` reads 8 bytes immediately before the PT_DYNAMIC array. ASan reports that pre-table address as a freed heap region in the reproduced run, producing the saved heap-use-after-free READ.

crash_location.function: unsigned long long get_ne64<void, void>(void const*)

allocation_context.description: ASan attributes the eventually-read address to a heap chunk allocated during the UPX doctest LZMA self-check that runs at the start of `upx_main()`.

free_context.description: The same doctest buffer is freed before the parser run. The vulnerable pre-table read in `elf_find_table_size()` later lands in that recycled freed region.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: ASan reports the inlined helper `get_ne64()` at `src/bele.h:124`, but the invalid address originates at `PackLinuxElf64::elf_find_table_size` line 7938 when `get_te64()` is asked to read `&dynseg[-1].d_val`.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation/free stacks belong to an earlier doctest LZMA buffer that happened to occupy the bytes immediately before `dynseg`; the source-level bug is still the unchecked zero sentinel in `dt_table[DT_SYMTAB]` that makes `elf_find_table_size()` read `dynseg[-1]`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_65765-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed the staged witness to the UPX `test_packed_file_fuzzer` harness and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` in `N_BELE_RTP::LEPolicy::get64` via `PackLinuxElf64::elf_find_table_size` and `PackLinuxElf64::invert_pt_dynamic`.

format.name: ELF64 little-endian ET_DYN shared object parsed by `upx -t`
format.contract: Exactly the staged 12248-byte witness `poc` with sha256 `1f15023f241827d2ecee608a2207cc5cedf1940f39dada21192f096277c3976e`. `file` and `readelf -h` identify it as an ELF64 little-endian shared object (`ET_DYN`) for x86-64. `readelf -d` shows a 17-entry dynamic section that ends at `DT_NULL` and contains `GNU_HASH`, `STRTAB`, `STRSZ`, `SYMENT`, `RELA`, `RELASZ`, `VERNEED`, `VERSYM`, and `RELACOUNT`, but no `DT_SYMTAB`. Under the fuzz target's `upx -t` path, UPX reaches `PackLinuxElf64help1`, scans that PT_DYNAMIC table, leaves `dt_table[DT_SYMTAB] == 0`, and still calls `elf_find_table_size(DT_SYMTAB, SHT_DYNSYM)`, which immediately turns the zero sentinel into the `dynseg[-1]` read. This contract is limited to the staged witness and observed `-t` parser mode, not all malformed ELF64 files that omit `DT_SYMTAB`.
